new.s: Which of the following antecedents of the Directive Principles gave the socialist-nationalist economic programme of the freedom struggle?
new.x: The Karachi Resolution of 1931 set out the socialist-nationalist economic programme of the freedom struggle, an Indian precursor of the DPSPs.
new.angle: U0289 notes gap: Karachi Resolution 1931 as DPSP antecedent

new.s: In which year was the Karachi Resolution, an Indian precursor of the Directive Principles, adopted?
new.x: The Karachi Resolution was adopted in 1931; the Nehru Report was 1928 and the Sapru Committee 1945.
new.angle: U0289 notes gap: Karachi Resolution year 1931

new.s: What were the Directive Principles called in the Irish Constitution of 1937, from which India borrowed them?
new.x: The Irish Constitution of 1937 called them 'Directive Principles of Social Policy'.
new.angle: U0289 notes gap: Irish name: Directive Principles of Social Policy

new.s: Which Article of the Constitution directs the State to secure the right to work, to education and to public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness and disablement?
new.x: Article 41 deals with the right to work, to education and to public assistance.
new.angle: U0289 notes gap: Art. 41 right to work and public assistance

new.s: Which Article of the Directive Principles directs the State to bring about prohibition of intoxicating drinks and drugs injurious to health?
new.x: Article 47 covers nutrition, public health and prohibition of intoxicating drinks and injurious drugs.
new.angle: U0289 notes gap: Art. 47 prohibition

new.s: Which Article of the Constitution directs the State to protect monuments and places of national importance?
new.x: Article 49, a Directive Principle, provides for the protection of monuments and places of national importance.
new.angle: U0289 notes gap: Art. 49 monuments

new.s: Which is the last Article of Part IV of the Constitution, dealing with the promotion of international peace and security?
new.x: Article 51, the last Article of Part IV, deals with international peace and security and respect for international law.
new.angle: U0289 notes gap: Art. 51 international peace, last article of Part IV

new.s: Article 48 directs the State to ban the slaughter of cows and calves. Under which entry does the power to legislate on this subject lie?
new.x: Article 48 is only a directive; the power to legislate on cow slaughter lies with the States under State List Entry 15 (livestock).
new.angle: U0289 notes gap: cow slaughter law power - State List Entry 15

new.s: Who said that the Directive Principles were 'no better than New Year's resolutions' which are broken on the second of January?
new.x: Nasiruddin compared the DPSPs to New Year's resolutions broken on the second of January.
new.angle: U0289 notes gap: Nasiruddin New Year's resolutions

new.s: Who described the Fundamental Rights and the Directive Principles together as the 'conscience of the Constitution'?
new.x: Granville Austin called the FRs and DPSPs together the 'conscience of the Constitution'.
new.angle: U0289 notes gap: Granville Austin conscience of the Constitution

new.s: Which State became the second State, after Uttarakhand, to move a State Uniform Civil Code?
new.x: Uttarakhand was the first State with a UCC and Gujarat the second; Goa follows the Portuguese Civil Code of 1867.
new.angle: U0289 notes gap: Gujarat second State UCC

new.s: Which Law Commission, headed by Justice B.S. Chauhan, said in 2018 that a Uniform Civil Code was 'neither necessary nor desirable'?
new.x: The 21st Law Commission under Justice B.S. Chauhan said in 2018 that a UCC was neither necessary nor desirable.
new.angle: U0289 notes gap: 21st Law Commission (B.S. Chauhan) on UCC

new.s: Which Act gives effect to Article 45 and Article 21A by providing free education to children aged 6-14 in a neighbourhood school?
o: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
new.x: The RTE Act, 2009 (Section 3) provides free education to children aged 6-14 in a neighbourhood school.
new.angle: U0289 notes gap: RTE Act 2009 implements 45/21A

new.s: Land reforms such as zamindari abolition and ceiling laws were enacted mainly to implement which Directive Principles?
new.x: Land reforms give effect to Articles 39(b) and 39(c) on distribution of material resources and preventing concentration of wealth.
new.angle: U0289 notes gap: land reforms implement 39(b),(c)

new.s: Before August 2019, which of the following Parts of the Constitution of India did not apply to the State of Jammu and Kashmir?
o: Part IV - Directive Principles of State Policy
Part XI - Relations between the Union and the States
new.x: Under the Constitution (Application to Jammu and Kashmir) Order, 1954, Part IV (DPSP) was not applicable to J&K, while Part III applied with modifications.
new.angle: U0289 web: PYQ ybb16dead219 DPSP not applicable to J&K

new.s: By which Presidential order of 5 August 2019 were all the provisions of the Constitution, including the Directive Principles, applied to Jammu and Kashmir?
o: Constitution (Application to Jammu and Kashmir) Order, 1954
Constitution (Application to Jammu and Kashmir) Order, 2019 (C.O. 272)
Constitution (One Hundred and Third Amendment) Act, 2019
new.x: C.O. 272 of 5 August 2019 superseded the 1954 Order and applied all provisions of the Constitution to J&K.
new.angle: U0289 web: PYQ ybb16dead219 C.O. 272 (2019) applied DPSP to J&K

new.s: Besides Article 13(4), which clause did the 24th Amendment, 1971 add to the Constitution?
new.x: The 24th Amendment added Articles 13(4) and 368(3); 368(4) and (5) came with the 42nd, and 31C with the 25th.
new.angle: U0290 notes gap: 24th added 13(4) and 368(3)

new.s: The Ninth Schedule, added in 1951 to protect agrarian reforms, has grown to about how many entries?
new.x: The Ninth Schedule grew to over 280 entries and is not limited to land reforms.
new.angle: U0290 notes gap: Ninth Schedule over 280 entries

new.s: Under which clause of Article 51A is it a Fundamental Duty to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India?
new.x: Article 51A(c) asks citizens to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India.
new.angle: U0291 notes gap: 51A(c) sovereignty clause

new.s: Under which clause of Article 51A is it a Fundamental Duty to defend the country and render national service when called upon?
new.x: Article 51A(d) is the duty to defend the country and render national service when called upon.
new.angle: U0291 notes gap: 51A(d) defend the country

new.s: Which clause of Article 51A asks citizens to strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity?
new.x: Article 51A(j) is the duty to strive towards excellence so that the nation rises to higher levels of endeavour.
new.angle: U0291 notes gap: 51A(j) excellence

new.s: In which year did the Justice J.S. Verma Committee on operationalising Fundamental Duties submit its work?
new.x: The J.S. Verma Committee on operationalising Fundamental Duties was in 1999; the Swaran Singh Committee was in 1976.
new.angle: U0291 notes gap: Verma Committee 1999

new.s: Imputations and assertions prejudicial to national integration, linked to the duty under Article 51A(c), are now an offence under which provision?
new.x: Such imputations are now punishable under Section 197 of the BNS, 2023 (earlier IPC Section 153B).
new.angle: U0291 notes gap: BNS Sec. 197 (old IPC 153B)

new.s: Who described the Indian Constitution as 'quasi-federal' and praised its balance between rigidity and flexibility?
new.x: K.C. Wheare called the Constitution quasi-federal and saw a good balance of rigidity and flexibility in its amendment procedure.
new.angle: U0292 notes gap: K.C. Wheare quasi-federal

new.s: Representation of States in Parliament, an amendment to which needs State ratification, is contained in which Schedule of the Constitution?
new.x: Representation of States in Parliament (Rajya Sabha seats) is in the Fourth Schedule, a federal provision needing ratification by half the States.
new.angle: U0292 notes gap: Fourth Schedule representation of States

new.s: Who was the Prime Minister when the First Constitutional Amendment, 1951 was enacted?
new.x: The First Amendment was enacted in 1951 under Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru.
new.angle: U0293 notes gap: 1st Amendment PM Nehru

new.s: Which body enacted the First Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951?
o: A joint sitting of both Houses
new.x: The First Amendment was enacted by the Provisional Parliament, before the first Lok Sabha was elected.
new.angle: U0293 notes gap: 1st Amendment by Provisional Parliament

new.s: Which Constitutional Amendment made the advice of the Council of Ministers binding on the President?
new.x: The 42nd Amendment, 1976 made ministerial advice binding on the President.
new.angle: U0293 notes gap: 42nd: ministerial advice binding

new.s: Why is the 42nd Amendment, 1976 called the 'Mini-Constitution'?
o: It changed the Preamble, the Seventh Schedule and 54 Articles
It replaced the whole Constitution of 1950
It was ratified by all the States
new.x: It is called the Mini-Constitution because it changed the Preamble, the Seventh Schedule and 54 Articles.
new.angle: U0293 notes gap: 42nd Mini-Constitution: 54 Articles

new.s: The 42nd Amendment froze the allocation of seats for delimitation on the basis of which Census?
new.x: The 42nd Amendment froze delimitation on the 1971 Census; the 84th later extended the freeze to 2026.
new.angle: U0293 notes gap: 42nd: delimitation frozen on 1971 Census

new.s:

2. The President may return the advice of the Council of Ministers once for reconsideration.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

new.s: On which date did the 61st Amendment, which lowered the voting age to 18, come into force?
new.x: The 61st Amendment came into force on 28 March 1989 and was first used in the 1989 general election.
new.angle: U0293 notes gap: 61st in force 28 March 1989

new.s: What did the 62nd Constitutional Amendment, 1989 provide for?
o: Extension of SC/ST seat reservation in legislatures to 2000
Lowering of the voting age to 18
new.x: The 62nd Amendment extended SC/ST seat reservation in the Lok Sabha and Assemblies up to 2000; anti-defection was the 52nd.
new.angle: U0293 notes gap: 62nd SC/ST seats to 2000

new.s: On which date did the 73rd Constitutional Amendment on Panchayats come into force?
new.x: The 73rd Amendment came into force on 24 April 1993; the 74th came into force on 1 June 1993.
new.angle: U0293 notes gap: 73rd in force 24 April 1993

new.s: On which date did the 74th Constitutional Amendment on Municipalities come into force?
new.x: The 74th Amendment (Part IXA, Twelfth Schedule) came into force on 1 June 1993.
new.angle: U0293 notes gap: 74th in force 1 June 1993

new.s: In which year did the Supreme Court strike down the 99th Amendment, which created the National Judicial Appointments Commission?
new.x: The 99th Amendment (2014) creating the NJAC was struck down in 2015 to protect judicial independence.
new.angle: U0293 notes gap: 99th NJAC struck down 2015

new.s: Which Constitutional Amendment gave constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes?
new.x: The 102nd Amendment, 2018 inserted Article 338B and made the NCBC a constitutional body.
new.angle: U0294 notes gap: 102nd NCBC constitutional status

new.s: From which date was the Goods and Services Tax, introduced by the 101st Amendment, rolled out?
new.x: The 101st Amendment got assent on 8 September 2016 and GST came into effect from 1 July 2017.
new.angle: U0294 notes gap: GST from 1 July 2017

new.s: Who chairs the GST Council under Article 279A?
o: The Chairman of the Finance Commission
new.x: The GST Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister and decides by a three-fourths majority.
new.angle: U0294 notes gap: GST Council chaired by Union FM

new.s: Under the 103rd Amendment, up to what household income limit is a family treated as Economically Weaker Section (EWS) for reservation?

new.angle: U0294 notes gap: EWS income limit Rs 8 lakh

new.s: Which recent Constitutional Amendment is the only one struck down as a whole by the Supreme Court?
new.x: The 99th Amendment (NJAC) was struck down as a whole; the 97th was struck down only in part (Rajendra N. Shah).
new.angle: U0294 notes gap: 99th only recent amendment struck down whole

new.s: Who chairs the Joint Parliamentary Committee examining the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 on One Nation, One Election?

notes.md: - **Jammu and Kashmir:** under the **Constitution (Application to Jammu and Kashmir) Order, 1954**, **Part IV (DPSP)** did not apply to J&K. The Presidential order **C.O. 272 of 5 August 2019** superseded the 1954 Order and applied **all provisions** of the Constitution to J&K.
